title: Walk on the artifact to see the whole
principle: Craig Mod’s essay To Make a Book, Walk on a Book: print/spread the work in physical space to see adjacencies a screen hides. For digital products, force a spatial review—spreads, storyboards, or wall printouts—before locking AI-generated flows.
procedure: Export key screens/pages at readable size.
Lay them out in order on a large surface (or infinite canvas zoomed out).
Walk the sequence; note broken adjacencies, pacing, and repeats.
Give the work time to sit—don’t rush the next AI iteration.
examplePrompts:
Prepare a walk-on-the-artifact review (Craig Mod):
- Export the flow as a single contact sheet / storyboard.
- Annotate adjacency problems and pacing issues.
- Propose reorder/cuts before any visual polish.
No endorsement.
Zoom out: show all primary screens at once; list what feels redundant when seen together.
tips: Physical print still best when possible.

workedExamples.title: On-screen tunnel vision
workedExamples.before: Each screen polished in isolation; flow repeats the same hero thrice.
workedExamples.after: Contact sheet cut two heroes; pacing breathes.
workedExamples.body: Adjacencies only appear in the spread.

workedExamples.title: Sit time
workedExamples.body: Leave the sheet overnight; morning edit is sharper than another AI pass.

antiPatterns: Pixel-polish one screen while the map is wrong.
Never viewing the product at overview scale.

inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Walk on the artifact to see the whole” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
1. Export key screens/pages at readable size.
2. Lay them out in order on a large surface (or infinite canvas zoomed out).
3. Walk the sequence; note broken adjacencies, pacing, and repeats.
4. Rearrange before polishing individual screens.
5. Give the work time to sit—don’t rush the next AI iteration.
acceptance: Show the before/after artifact and explain how “Walk on the artifact to see the whole” improves the named user task.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
